The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries suffered by her in a road traffic accident dated 03.06.2020.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, On 01.02.2019 at about 11.30am, when she was riding her scooter from Doddabidrakallu to Nagasandra Main Road, near Venkateswara Bekary, an Auto bearing Reg.No.KA41 4114 came from her back side in a high speed rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner.
As a result the SCCH - 25 3 MVC No.1352/2019 petitioner has sustained injuries over head and other parts of the body.
3. It is the further case of the petitioner that, after the accident she was shifted to People Tree Hospital, Goregunte Palya, Bangalore and she has taken treatment.
Before the accident she was hale and healthy, aged about 39 years working as a Tailor and earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
After the accident due to the disability she is unable to continue her work and the injuries have led to loss of income.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the Auto driver.
The Peenya Traffic police have registered a case against him.
1 St respondent being the RC Owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the Auto are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
4. In response to notice issued by this Tribunal, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels.
But the respondent No.2 alone filed written statement.
The objections of the Respondent No.2.
It has denied all the averments of the petition except issuance of insurance policy in favour of the Autorickshaw.

The petitioner was riding the alleged Scooter in a rash and negligent manner without knowledge of driving, nor wearing helmet and without a valid DL and she has collided with a Four wheeler and there was no involvement of Autorickshaw i.e. the insured vehicle.
The 1 st respondent knowingly entrusted the insured vehicle to the Driver who had no valid and effective DL and has consciously breached the terms and conditions of the policy.
The petition is bad for noncompliance of Sec.158(6) and 134(C) of MV Act and also for non joinder of necessary parties.
The accident is solely due to the negligence of the petitioner herself.
It also denied age, occupation and the manner of accident.
It contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate.

Therefore,
prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:

Issue No.1: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Autorickshaw, the petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.8.
She has reiterated the contents of the petition in her affidavit filed in lieu of her chief examination.

During her cross examination the counsel for the Respondent No.2 got marked 2 documents as per Exs.R.1 & R.2 i.e., statement of victim given to the police and MLC pertaining to the People Tree Hospital, Dasarahalli.
She has admitted that as per Ex.P.5 the front portion of her scooter was damaged.

On the other hand the respondent No.2 has contended that the Autorickshaw Prema.T.C vs Krishnamurthy Eshwar Naik on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166675397/

sentences.text: In support of the same, they got examined the MRO of People Tree hospital as RW.1 and got marked Exs.R.1 to 3 (2 documents were already marked through PW.1 during her cross examination, these numbering of documents is repeated).
Ex.R.1 is authorization letter, Ex.R.2 is true copy of SCCH - 25 8 MVC No.1352/2019 MLC and R.3 is the police intimation.
During his cross the petitioner has got marked a document as per Ex.P.22.

The Respondent No.2 has also got examined Investigation Officer of the case as RW.2 who has stated that even though there was a mistake in the registration number of the Two wheeler involved in the accident, since the vehicle was present at the spot, he did not investigate about the same and only recorded the further statement of the complainant.
He has admitted that in Ex.R.2 it is written that the two wheeler collided with a Four wheeler.
During his crossexamination by the counsel for the petitioner, he has stated that in the police intimation it is written that the Two wheeler is hit by Three wheeler.
11. The accident occurred on 01.02.2019 at 11.30am as per the petition averments as well as the complaint marked at Ex.P.2 and the FIR was registered on the same day at 3.00pm.

The respondent No.2 has contended that the registration number of the Two wheeler given in Ex.P.2 is different from the registration number of the vehicle involved SCCH - 25 9 MVC No.1352/2019 in the accident.

However, the same complainant, who is none other than the husband of the petitioner has given additional statement as per Ex.P.3 stating about the same mistake and it can be seen that the additional statement is also given on the same day.
As per Ex.P.4 the Panchanama was also conducted on the same day from 5.00 to 6.00pm.
Though there is no mention about the seizure of the vehicle at Panchanama the Investigation Officer - RW.2 has stated that he seized the vehicle from the spot.
12. According to Ex.P.5, the Autorickshaw was damaged to the left side rear wheel, whereas the Two wheeler was damaged to the front shape right side scratched.
This shows that the Autorickshaw's rear left side hit to the front right side of the Two wheeler.
As per the case of the petitioner the Autorickshaw hit her scooter from behind and the same is shown in the Sketch at Ex.P.6 also.
However in the complaint at Ex.P.2 and in the FIR it is mentioned that the Autorickshaw was coming from the opposite direction.
However from the SCCH - 25 10 MVC No.1352/2019 damages mentioned at Ex.P.5 it is clear that the Autorickshaw could have come from the behind only for the kind of damages suffered by the vehicle.
As per Ex.P.7 the petitioner has suffered injuries in a RTA and the police have filed the charge sheet against the driver of the Autorickshaw as per Ex.P.8.
The main contention of the Respondent No.2 is about the change of the vehicle number in the complaint and FIR and in the charge sheet.
However, to clear the same, the complainant i.e., the husband of the petitioner has given an additional statement as per Ex.P.3.
Moreover, during the examination of the IO as RW.2, he has stated that there was no confusion with regard to the registration number of the victim's vehicle since it was there on the spot.
13. Another contention of the respondent No.2 is that in one of the MLCs it is mentioned as the petitioner is hit by Four wheeler.

However, at this point of time it should be noted that in all the other documents i.e., Ex.P.10 - Discharge summary of People Tree hospital, Goraguntepalya, MLC register extract SCCH - 25 11 MVC No.1352/2019 of People Tree hospital, Goraguntepalya at Ex.P.18, police intimation of People Tree hospital, Goraguntepalya at Ex.P.19, A & E Trauma report Prema.T.C vs Krishnamurthy Eshwar Naik on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166675397/
4 at Ex.P.22 which was marked through RW.1 by the counsel for the petitioner which shows that the petitioner was hit by a Three wheeler.

Therefore, on perusal of all the documents it is clear that except Ex.R.2 marked on 29.09.2021 through Pw.1 i.e., the MLC register extract of Raghavendra People Tree Hospitals, all the other documents show it as petitioner being hit by the Three wheeler.
It is admitted by the petitioner herself that first she was admitted to Raghavendra People Tree Hospital, Dasarahalli and later she was shifted to the People Tree Hospital, Goraguntepalya.
However, this shifting of the petitioner was done on the same day within a few hours.
Moreover the FIR was registered within a few hours and the vehicles were also seized on the same day.

Wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court India has held that based on the facts of the case that contributory negligence can be taken.
However as discussed above, there are no glaring mistakes and there is no suspicious circumstances for the change of Four wheeler to Three wheeler in the MLC register extracts.
Therefore, the above said decisions are not applicable to this case.
On perusal of all the documents on record it is clear that the accident was caused by the driver of the Autorickshaw.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

15. In support of the same she has examined Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao as PW.3 and got marked 3 documents as SCCH - 25 14 MVC No.1352/2019 per Exs.P.23 to 25 i.e., OPD record, Neuro Psychological Assessment report and Mini Mental State Examination.
The doctor has given the details of the problem and stated that her whole body disability is at 10%.
During his cross examination he has admitted that the head injury needs continuous treatment.
He has stated that even though the GCS score has improved, her IQ was 85 as per neuronpsychological assessment report.
According to the petitioner she was working as a Tailor and earning Rs.15,000/ per month.

It can be seen on perusal of the MMSE report that she is suffering from short term loss of memory,
attention deficit and there is mild cognitive impairment.
Therefore, the Tribunal deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 10%.

Monthly income:
16.
The Petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, she was working as a Tailor and earning Rs.15,000/ per month.
To substantiate the income, the Petitioner neither produced any documents nor examined any witness SCCH - 25 15 MVC No.1352/2019
Therefore, the version of the Petitioner that she was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month, is not acceptable.
Therefore, the notional income needs to be considered.
The Tribunal deems it fit to fix the monthly notional income of the petitioner as Rs.14,000/ per month.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 41 years as could be made out from Ex.P.9/Aadhar card of the petitioner.
The accident took place in the year 2019.

As such, Petitioner is entitled for the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at People Tree hospital as an inpatient from 01.02.2019 to 05.02.2019, discharged with advice to take follow up treatment.
In this regard, she has produced Ex.P.10 Discharge summary issued by People Tree Hospital.
Considering that the nature of injuries she has undergone is grievous, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/ under this head.
SCCH - 25 16 MVC No.1352/2019  ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that she has spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/ towards hospitalization,
medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, she has produced 18 medical bills as per Ex.P.13 for a sum of Rs.77,115/.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondents.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner has taken treatment for 5 days at People Tree Hospital which can be made out from Exs.P.7 & 10 wound certificate and Discharge summary.

Therefore,

SCCH - 25 17 MVC No.1352/2019 Hence, she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.14,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME: On perusal of Ex.P.9, as on the date of accident she was 41 years old.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable for her age is 14.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.2,35,200/ (Rs.14,000/ x 12 x 14 x 10%= Rs.2,35,200/) under this head.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 41 years at the time of accident.
She has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, she is suffering from 10% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout her life.
Because of this she will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age SCCH - 25 18 MVC No.1352/2019 and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/ is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospital, admitted for 5 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period she must have spent considerable amount on her food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/
under this head.

17. The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.1,00,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs.77,115/
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.14,000/ period 4. Loss of future income Rs.2,35,200/
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/ happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges TOTAL Rs.4,66,315/ SCCH - 25 19 MVC No.1352/2019
If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.4,66,400/ and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.

7 LIABILITY 18.
The respondent No.2 has examined its Senior Executive Legal as RW.3.

He has filed affidavit in lieu of his chief examination by reiterating the contentions in the written statement and got marked 3 documents as per Exs.R.1 to 3 i.e., the authorization letter, true copy of insurance policy and letter sent to insured along with returned postal cover with postal receipt and acknowledgment.
During his crossexamination nothing worthwhile is elicited.
The Respondent No.2 has not proved the defence taken by them in their written statement.
Therefore, the respondent Nos.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the insurance company i.e., Respondent No.2 is directed to SCCH - 25 20 MVC No.1352/2019 indemnify the respondent No.1 since the policy was in existence as on the date of accident.
The petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.25,00,000/ but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.4,66,400/ with interest @6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to allowed.
Accordingly, issue No.2 held in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,66,400/ (Rupees Four Lakhs Sixty Six Thousand Four Hundred only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till SCCH - 25 21 MVC No.1352/2019 the date of depositing the amount.
The respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
